title: Church, hymns and funeral music
summary: Her Creole family was Baptist and Catholic, Joe's mother was Baptist, Joe loved hymns, and bands played hymns at funerals.

story.theme_name: Church, faith and religion in a musician's life
story.community_name: Church, faith and jazz: the sacred and the secular

blocks.x: Do you remember any parades? Did they have any brass bands on the streets? Any parades when you were a girl?
In Donaldsonville? No. No, we didn't have that.
I wondered about the music and the churches too.
Oh yes, yes. We had churches and all of my family belonged to church. And they used to have baptizing.
That's a Baptist church. But my family is Creole. So we mixed up. Some are Baptist and some are Catholic.
You know what, did Joe belong to any church? Do you remember?
He never did belong to any church, but his mother was Baptist.
His father was probably a Baptist preacher.

Yes, that's right. That's right. And Joe is always crazy about the hymns. And he used to kid me and laugh. He'd take some of the hymns and make some songs with it. But finally, they did, eventually they did because when the saints were marching in, that was a hymn.
All those numbers, I close your walk and glory land, they used by and by.
Did Joe play many of those tunes ever? Oh yes.

Yes. No, but they played them when they, you know, when they went to bury anybody. Yes, on the funerals. Yeah, on the funerals. They would play, they would play, take them to the funeral, they would play hymns. And when they come back, they would play hymns. And when they come back,
